doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

chapter: The music business then and now
title: The segregated black musicians' union in Chicago
summary: Local 208 was the separate black local, merged into Local 10 in the 1960s as integration spread.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Can I wind you back for a minute?
You said going back to Chicago. And you talked about the musician’s union and you said there was a black musician’s union. This was separate?
And how, when did that like stop?
I don’t know the exact year. But I guess it stopped in the 60’s.

Where they dissolved the black unions into the, for example in Chicago it was Local 10. And Local 10 took over 208 and I think a couple of the executives in 208 became, you know, because part of Local 10’s hierarchy in other words, the people that took care of the business of the union. And in California, 47 was the major union and I’m trying to remember what number the black union was, but anyway they all integrated. Like it was a whole period of when all this integration started up in the schools and the whole thing, around that time.
